newsitem.title: CANADA: Nortel to invest $125 mln in Brazil plant.
newsitem.headline: Nortel to invest $125 mln in Brazil plant.

text.p: Northern Telecom Ltd said it was chosen to provide telecommunications equipment and services worth $300 million in Brazil and plans to invest $125 million in a Sao Paulo plant.

A consortium led by U.S.-based BellSouth Corp granted Nortel, Canada's largest telecommunications firm, part of a $2.45 billion contract to provide the city of Sao Paulo with a cellular telephone network, Nortel said in a conference call.
The company estimated the contract was one of the largest such deals awarded outside the United States.
Last year Nortel had a $1 billion deal with Sprint.
Nortel will design, build and commission a digital cellular network to serve the greater Sao Paulo metropolitan area starting in 1998.
"Over the next ten years, as network capacity is expanded and more customers are served, the value of the contract could increase," Nortel said in a statement.

The consortium, which includes Banco Safra, media group O Estado de Sao Paulo and telecommunications equipment maker Splice, all of Brazil, beat out six other groups for the 20-year concession from the Communications Ministry on Wednesday.

Also, Nortel will make digital wireless telecommunications systems starting in 1997's fourth quarter at a Campinas, Sao Paulo State plant in concert with Brazilian engineering firm Promon Eletronica. Its initial investment will total more than $25 million in manufacturing and $100 million in other operations such as training, research and development.
